Observation: Reference model: validation MSE 358.80 kg². Used as the comparison benchmark for all neural networks.
Baseline NN reduced validation MSE compared with linear regression. Best checkpoint was epoch 41; early stopping ended training at epoch 51.
Very small learning rate; still improving at the 100-epoch limit, with high validation MSE. Consistent with slow convergence under the training budget.
Improved substantially over A01, but best performance was near the 100-epoch cap and remained worse than baseline; suggests relatively slow convergence.
Approached baseline validation performance, but required 94 epochs to reach its best checkpoint, indicating slower progress than the baseline learning rate.
Validation MSE came close to baseline but best checkpoint was reached later (epoch 85); lower learning rate may need more epochs to settle.
Reached near-baseline validation MSE by epoch 18 and stopped at 28; faster progress, with slightly worse best MSE than baseline.
Reached its best validation score very early (epoch 10); faster apparent convergence, but slightly worse MSE than baseline.
Larger learning rate produced worse validation MSE than moderate rates; oversized updates may have limited optimization quality. Confirm stability from the loss curve.
Momentum 0.5 achieved validation performance very close to baseline at an earlier best epoch (26 vs 41). The small MSE difference is not conclusive.
Momentum 0.9 reached near-baseline validation performance at epoch 21, suggesting faster convergence; result was virtually tied with momentum 0.5.
High momentum gave worse validation MSE; excessive accumulated updates may impair stability at the fixed learning rate. Inspect the curve before claiming instability.
Adam reached its best checkpoint quickly (epoch 6) but underperformed SGD at the same learning rate. This does not show Adam is generally worse at its own tuned rate.
AdamW reached best validation performance by epoch 6, but its MSE was higher than baseline; optimizer-specific learning rate/weight decay may matter.
Training with L1 achieved a slightly worse validation MSE than training with MSE. All runs were still evaluated using original-scale MSE.
Huber delta 0.5 achieved validation MSE close to baseline, with its best checkpoint at epoch 62. Delta was applied to the standardized target.
Huber delta 2.0 was the strongest alternative loss configuration among A13–A15, though still slightly worse than baseline MSE training.
